licensed features require a fresh HTTPS: licensed features require a fresh HTTPS time check on each application start. The check reads time headers from Microsoft and Google without sending names, machine IDs or project data to those sites. Two available responses must agree within five minutes; if only one succeeds it is used. Invalid responses, blocked HTTPS or certificate failures leave Licensed unavailable until a successful Recheck license time. After verification, Windows' monotonic uptime counter advances license time through sleep and hibernation, independently of the editable calendar clock. An open session retries time checks hourly and permits at most twenty-four hours without a new successful check. Moving Windows time backward does not extend the license. A protected high-water time record also rejects stale responses. Expiry is checked during use and before licensed operations; files already being committed finish safely. No desktop-only license scheme can fully resist an administrator patching the executable, stealing owner keys or restoring an entire virtual machine snapshot. A future account website can add signed server leases, revocation and balance billing. The current owner keygen already records request creation, owner receipt and license issue/expiry as JSONL for that integration. Keep the owner signing and request-decryption keys private and export their password-encrypted backup from the keygen before moving to another PC.

Encryption is optional; compression-only folder sync does not require a project key or encryption license. A conditional commit index defines causal order. Unreferenced or partially uploaded files are never committed. Clients use a local checkpoint and download only missing batches without scanning the entire history. An unchanged sync does not rewrite the local project or create a full local backup. Transactions retain stable record IDs, previous and new values, original available authors, UTC times and causal revision references. Unknown authors remain Unknown. Equipment assignment conflicts and complex simultaneous workbook layout or dictionary changes may require reconciliation. Only when it is enabled does the client read and reconcile the legacy single-file backup against its imported ancestor; identical imports are deduplicated. Restore as new project chooses a destination; Merge into current project reviews conflicts and backs up current work. Required hashes, project identity, exact snapshot event coverage and native workbook/drawing resources are checked before saving. A damaged latest snapshot can fall back to an earlier valid snapshot and replay retained batches only when the exact current state can be reconstructed. Required missing data stops recovery. History is never automatically deleted. Local storage, in-memory navigation and the existing native-part recovery journal remain unchanged; existing local encryption is preserved even when shared sync uses compression only. Save a new project first so its journal has a file location. Sync and backup processing run on background workers without a database migration.

Select a policy row and open Policy. Set: Select a policy row and open Policy. Set target stock, safety stock, manual weekly demand, planned campaign demand, forecast period and forecast mode. Physical minimum is a stock threshold. Reorder point is the greater of that minimum and safety stock plus expected demand during lead time plus planned demand. Safety stock defaults to the minimum, so the same buffer is not added twice. Suggested order quantity considers available stock, outstanding orders, the reorder point and target stock. Planned demand is treated as already allocated; do not include it twice. Manual or Campaign planning is preferred for irregular drilling demand. History forecasting is opt-in, uses weighted 30, 90 and 180-day net consumption and requires at least three consumption dates spanning 30 days. Returns net against matching prior well and serial consumption. Transfers, reservations, receipts and adjustments are not consumption. Without adequate history, the application states Insufficient consumption history. Dated incoming orders are applied to projected stock; a forecast stockout before delivery is critical. Red means critical shortage or timing risk, yellow means action or partial coverage, blue means a physical shortage covered by dated incoming orders, and green means the configured policy is met.

Charts show net consumption versus receipts, supplier deliveries, actual versus promised lead times, stock coverage, risk distribution, ordering efficiency, movement trends and projected balances. Click a PN chart row to navigate to its Min. Stock policy. Supplier performance uses actual order, promised and receipt dates, with partial delivery lines labelled separately. Planning lead time never substitutes for actual supplier performance. Unsupported metrics show an empty state; ordering efficiency needs recorded decision history. Autofill is the table-with-sparkle icon:

Autofill can use an approved dated equipment requirement in the active schedule scenario, or a dated upcoming drilling activity plus sufficient historical installation evidence. An approved requirement needs a valid PN, a positive quantity and a readiness date that is not in the past. Proposed or rejected requirements are not accepted as confirmed demand. Cancelled, completed, postponed and summary activities are excluded.
For historical estimates, eligible reference wells are distinct named wells with valid spud and end dates, an end date on or before today, and an end date no earlier than spud. At least three distinct completed wells must span 30 days by spud date. Each suggested historical PN also needs at least three positive examples spanning 30 days. These are minimum evidence checks, not a guarantee of statistical reliability. A blank or unverified equipment slot is excluded rather than counted as zero demand. Operational dates estimate consumption timing; they are not actual stock-movement timestamps.
The default opens and calculates automatically using eligible history and the current rig schedule. No manual well selection is required. Use selected historical wells only is an optional override; the same sufficiency checks apply to the selected subset. Change forecast start or the 1–520 week horizon, then Analyze references to recalculate. The default horizon is 52 weeks. The tool uses the active schedule scenario. A period with no supported demand shows an explanation rather than invented recommendations.
Historical PN mix is calculated within each standard equipment slot from positive verified PN records. A PN observed on 6 of 10 positive slot records contributes an estimated 0.6 units per future drilling well, not one unit on every well. Different variants are therefore not all assumed to be installed on each future well. PNs below the minimum evidence threshold are omitted without redistributing their share. If a scheduled region is specified, only matching historical region records are used; recognized Black Sea and Mediterranean names are normalized. If region/design is unspecified, pooled historical PN mix is labeled lower-confidence and requires an applicability review. Historic designs are not inferred from filenames or serial numbers.
Only included dated drilling activities contribute to historical estimates. Completion, rig moves and maintenance do not automatically consume drilling hardware. A repeated named planned well is counted once. Explicit approved equipment requirements take precedence for an activity; historical estimates are not added to the same activity, so partial approved plans still require a completeness review. The Approved schedule requirements mode restricts the calculation to explicit approved demand. Exact, month and quarter schedule dates retain their stored precision; earliest plausible starts are used for conservative timing.
For permanent equipment, expected quantities are grouped by PN and projected onto schedule dates. The recommendation is the ceiling of peak demand within a replenishment window plus configured safety stock. A known requirement/policy lead time defines the window; the largest known lead time for that PN is used. If no lead time is known, the selected forecast horizon is explicitly used as a planning assumption; supplier lead time is left unfilled. Reusable equipment uses peak concurrent units between planned start and finish, not permanent consumption. Without a finish date its occupancy is held indefinitely. Mixed reusable/permanent classification and duplicate policies for one PN are omitted for manual resolution.

Current stock and open orders are not subtracted from a minimum physical-stock threshold. Use the separate schedule procurement view for dated stock allocation and proposed order quantities; an Autofill threshold is not itself an order quantity.
Apply changes only selected stock policies, fills unknown policy lead time only when supported, and can add missing PN policies. It does not approve schedule BOM items, place orders, assign serial numbers, record receipts or consume inventory. One Undo reverses the batch; Redo restores it. Normal named revision history records the changes. Native policy values and supporting revision history survive project save, synchronization and licensed Excel export. A manually entered minimum below the last reviewed recommendation glows with a hover explanation. That warning refers to the last reviewed calculation; rerun Autofill when history, programme or assumptions change.

Actual consumption movement forecasting in the separate policy engine has its own data requirements. A sufficient-evidence flag permits a reviewable estimate; it does not imply that a forecast is factual or high-confidence. Declare Beyond Economical Repair records:

Approve for Scrap is a separate named approval; it does not mean the equipment has physically left the stock location and does not reduce physically held stock. The item remains in Quarantine with Approved for Scrap disposition until disposal is actually completed.
Complete Disposal requires the separate scrap-approved predecessor, a reason, evidence/reference and a dedicated named confirmation. It removes only the completed quantity from active physical/available/incoming stock and retains PN, SN, location, documents and lifecycle events. A partial nonserialized disposal splits a child identity, leaving the remaining quantity intact. The disposed item moves out of the active Quarantine view into Disposed archive, which is audit-only.
Ordinary edits, transfers and Undo cannot make a disposed item available again. Use a documented Reverse Disposal action with confirmation and evidence if a disposal was recorded incorrectly. It preserves the original disposal and returns only to unavailable Pending Assessment; it does not skip inspection/testing or release approval. The reversal itself is also protected from ordinary Undo. Source records and histories are preserved rather than overwritten. This workflow records declared approvals; it does not implement future RBAC or verify external physical-disposal evidence.
